exposure: antenatal fetal weight estimation (suspected FGR vs. no suspicion)
suspected FGR and birth weight (true positive, false positive, true negative, false negative)
outcome: neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rate
finding: Antenatal diagnosis of fetal growth restriction (FGR) was independently associated with a 70% increased risk of cesarean delivery in neonates who were appropriate for gestational age (AGA), without improvement in neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Suspicion of FGR was independently associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery among neonates who were ultimately classified as AGA.
birth_weight: Included in analysis, categorized as SGA or AGA
